selected.title: El Niño-linked ocean wave could raise West Coast sea levels this month
selected.summary: A series of warm-water Kelvin waves is expected to raise sea levels along the West Coast by several inches and potentially up to a foot. Higher baseline water levels could compound high tides, large swells and storms, increasing erosion and coastal flooding risks. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/52246a73e6842e4561b5195df526dd8e?utm_source=openai))
selected.why_it_matters: The temporary rise may stress beaches, coastal infrastructure and flood defenses before the region’s winter storm season. It illustrates how ocean dynamics can amplify familiar coastal hazards without a major storm arriving first.
selected.butterfly_question: How might a temporary rise in coastal water levels change the impact of this winter’s storms?

selected.title: Amazon pledges $1 billion for communities hosting its data centers
selected.summary: Amazon says it will invest more than $1 billion over five years in U.S. communities where it operates data centers, funding areas including education, job training, water and energy initiatives. The announcement comes amid growing local opposition to data-center construction and its effects on electricity, water and communities. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/91b65ba1729540c1c0d92e35deef35d8?utm_source=openai))
selected.why_it_matters: The plan makes local acceptance and community benefits a more visible part of the economics of AI infrastructure. Whether the pledge changes siting decisions or local opposition could shape the pace and terms of future data-center expansion.
selected.butterfly_question: Will community investment become a standard cost of building large-scale AI infrastructure?

selected.title: Roman telescope’s planet-imaging coronagraph takes its first space image
selected.summary: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope coronagraph successfully captured its first image of cosmic light after demonstrating steady pointing and focus. The instrument is a technology demonstration designed to block starlight so that much fainter planets and disks around nearby stars can be imaged. ([jpl.nasa.gov](https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/nasas-roman-team-snaps-test-coronagraph-image/?utm_source=openai))
selected.why_it_matters: The test advances techniques that could enable future missions to directly study planets around other stars, including worlds more Earth-like than those the instrument itself is designed to demonstrate. It also marks an early commissioning milestone for a major new observatory.
selected.butterfly_question: What technologies proven on Roman could make direct studies of potentially habitable worlds possible?

sources.title: NASA’s Roman Team Snaps Test Coronagraph Image

selected.title: G7 agrees to release 100 million barrels of oil and fuel products
selected.summary: G7 members plan a coordinated release of 100 million barrels of oil and fuel products over four months, with substantial diesel volumes front-loaded, as fuel prices surge. The agreement also includes a pledge to avoid energy export restrictions. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/774a360d1646d9ce8aba764fdd9959d2?utm_source=openai))
selected.why_it_matters: The move links strategic reserves, fuel affordability and international trade coordination at a time of supply pressure. Its market effect will depend on how quickly the fuel reaches buyers and whether the underlying supply disruption eases.
selected.butterfly_question: Could the coordinated release ease prices—or mainly buy time for governments and fuel markets?

selected.title: Study reopens possibility that animals evolved far earlier than their fossils show
selected.summary: A new molecular-clock analysis argues that animals may have originated roughly 800–700 million years ago, as much as 200 million years before the oldest definitive animal body fossils. The authors emphasize that the analysis does not prove animals existed that early; it challenges assumptions used to set upper age limits from gaps in the fossil record. ([eurekalert.org](https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/1145493?utm_source=openai))
selected.why_it_matters: If supported by further evidence, the finding would change the timeline scientists use to study early animal evolution and Earth’s ancient ecosystems. It also highlights how fossil preservation gaps can shape estimates of life’s history.
selected.butterfly_question: What new fossils or molecular evidence could confirm—or rule out—such an early animal origin?
